claim: Tbx3 and Tbx5 are located in cis within 0.6 Mb on chromosome 5 in mice.
source: Tbx3 and Tbx5 are situated in cis within 0.6 Mb on chromosome 5 in mice, rendering their simultaneous deletion unattainable with the available single allele conditional alleles.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a factual statement about the genomic location of these genes.

claim: The cardiac conduction system orchestrates electrical impulses that enable coordinated contraction of cardiac chambers.
source: The cardiac conduction system (CCS) orchestrates the electrical impulses that enable coordinated contraction of the cardiac chambers.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the function of the CCS.

claim: TBX3 and TBX5 are required for CCS development.
source: The T-box transcription factors TBX3 and TBX5 are required for CCS development and associated with overlapping and distinct human CCS diseases.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: TBX3 and TBX5 are associated with overlapping and distinct human CCS diseases.
source: The T-box transcription factors TBX3 and TBX5 are required for CCS development and associated with overlapping and distinct human CCS diseases.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by references to human genetic studies.

claim: Conditional deletion of both Tbx3 and Tbx5 in the VCS using MinKCreERT2 caused loss of VCS function and molecular identity.
source: Conditional deletion of both T-box transcriptional factors in the VCS, using the VCS-specific MinKCreERT2, caused loss of VCS function and molecular identity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Combined Tbx3 and Tbx5 deficiency in the adult VCS led to prolonged PR intervals.
source: Combined Tbx3 and Tbx5 deficiency in the adult VCS led to conduction defects, including prolonged PR and QRS intervals and elevated susceptibility to ventricular tachycardia.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 2A with quantitative data.

claim: Combined Tbx3 and Tbx5 deficiency in the adult VCS led to prolonged QRS intervals.
source: Combined Tbx3 and Tbx5 deficiency in the adult VCS led to conduction defects, including prolonged PR and QRS intervals and elevated susceptibility to ventricular tachycardia.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 2A with quantitative data.

claim: Combined Tbx3 and Tbx5 deficiency in the adult VCS led to elevated susceptibility to ventricular tachycardia.
source: Combined Tbx3 and Tbx5 deficiency in the adult VCS led to conduction defects, including prolonged PR and QRS intervals and elevated susceptibility to ventricular tachycardia.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 2G and 2H with quantitative data.

claim: Electrophysiological defects in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout mice occurred prior to detectable alterations in cardiac contractility.
source: These electrophysiological defects occurred prior to detectable alterations in cardiac contractility or histologic morphology, indicative of a primary conduction system defect.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by echocardiography data in Figure 3.

claim: Electrophysiological defects in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout mice occurred prior to detectable alterations in histologic morphology.
source: These electrophysiological defects occurred prior to detectable alterations in cardiac contractility or histologic morphology, indicative of a primary conduction system defect.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by histological analysis in Figure 3G-K.

claim: The electrophysiological defects in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout mice are indicative of a primary conduction system defect.
source: These electrophysiological defects occurred prior to detectable alterations in cardiac contractility or histologic morphology, indicative of a primary conduction system defect.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the abstract based on the temporal relationship between conduction defects and structural changes.

claim: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout VCS cardiomyocytes revealed a transcriptional shift toward non-CCS-specialized working myocardium.
source: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout VCS cardiomyocytes revealed a transcriptional shift toward non-CCS-specialized working myocardium, indicating a change to their cellular identity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by qRT-PCR and Western blot data in Figure 4.

claim: The transcriptional shift in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout VCS cardiomyocytes indicates a change to their cellular identity.
source: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout VCS cardiomyocytes revealed a transcriptional shift toward non-CCS-specialized working myocardium, indicating a change to their cellular identity.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the abstract based on the transcriptional data.

claim: Optical mapping revealed a loss of VCS-specific conduction system propagation in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout mice.
source: Furthermore, optical mapping revealed a loss of VCS-specific conduction system propagation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 5 with optical mapping data.

claim: Tbx3 and Tbx5 coordinate to control VCS molecular fate and function.
source: Collectively, these findings indicate that Tbx3 and Tbx5 coordinate to control VCS molecular fate and function, with implications for understanding cardiac conduction disorders in humans.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the collective experimental findings.

claim: The mature mammalian CCS can be divided into slowly propagating atrial nodes (~5 cm/s) and rapidly propagating ventricular conduction system (~200 cm/s).
source: In the mature mammalian heart, the functional components of the CCS can be broadly divided into the slowly propagating atrial nodes (~5 cm/s), containing the sinoatrial node (SAN) and atrioventricular node (AVN), and the rapidly propagating ventricular conduction system (VCS) (~200 cm/s), including the AV (His) bundle and the right and left bundle branches (BBs).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with specific conduction velocities and supported by citations.

claim: The VCS is responsible for rapid propagation of electrical impulse from the AVN to the ventricular apex.
source: The VCS is responsible for rapid propagation of the electrical impulse from the AVN to the ventricular apex to enable synchronous ventricular contraction and effective ejection of blood from the ventricles (Arnolds et al., 2012; Park and Fishman, 2011; Moskowitz et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The VCS enables synchronous ventricular contraction and effective ejection of blood from the ventricles.
source: The VCS is responsible for rapid propagation of the electrical impulse from the AVN to the ventricular apex to enable synchronous ventricular contraction and effective ejection of blood from the ventricles (Arnolds et al., 2012; Park and Fishman, 2011; Moskowitz et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Defects of CCS can occur in normally formed hearts as well as in patients with structural congenital heart disease.
source: Defects of CCS can occur in normally formed hearts as well as in patients with structural congenital heart disease and are a major source of morbidity and mortality (Arnolds et al., 2012; Moskowitz et al., 2007; Munshi, 2012; Rubart and Zipes, 2005; Huikuri et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CCS defects are a major source of morbidity and mortality.
source: Defects of CCS can occur in normally formed hearts as well as in patients with structural congenital heart disease and are a major source of morbidity and mortality (Arnolds et al., 2012; Moskowitz et al., 2007; Munshi, 2012; Rubart and Zipes, 2005; Huikuri et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The VCS has been recognized as a substrate for life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.
source: The VCS specifically has been recognized as a substrate for life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias, including bundle branch reentry tachycardia, idiopathic fascicular tachycardia, short-coupled torsade de pointes, and ventricular fibrillation (Arnolds et al., 2012; Huikuri et al., 2001; van Duijvenboden et al., 2014; Arnolds and Moskowitz, 2011b; Scheinman, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Human genetic studies have identified Tbx3 and Tbx5 as loci associated with adult human CCS function.
source: Human genetic studies have identified numerous loci associated with adult human CCS function, including the developmentally important factors Tbx3 and Tbx5 (reviewed in Arnolds et al., 2012; Arnolds et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Tbx3 and Tbx5 play crucial roles in adult CCS development and function.
source: Tbx3 and Tbx5 play crucial roles in adult CCS development and function (Arnolds et al., 2012; Moskowitz et al., 2007; Burnicka-Turek et al., 2020; Moskowitz et al., 2004; van Weerd and Christoffels, 2016; van den Boogaard et al., 2012; Bakker et al., 2012; Hatcher and Basson, 2009; Bakker et al., 2008; Hoogaars et al., 2007b; Mori et al., 2006; Bruneau et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with extensive supporting citations.

claim: Tbx5 encodes a T-box transcriptional activator required for structural and conduction system cardiac development.
source: Tbx5 encodes a T-box transcriptional activator required for structural and conduction system cardiac development (Moskowitz et al., 2007; Moskowitz et al., 2004; Bruneau et al., 2001; Hoogaars et al., 2007a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Dominant mutations in human TBX5 cause Holt–Oram syndrome.
source: Dominant mutations in human TBX5 cause Holt–Oram syndrome (HOS, OMIM:142900), an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by upper limb malformations, congenital heart defects, and CCS abnormalities (Basson et al., 1997; Li et al., 1997; Basson et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Holt–Oram syndrome is characterized by upper limb malformations, congenital heart defects, and CCS abnormalities.
source: Dominant mutations in human TBX5 cause Holt–Oram syndrome (HOS, OMIM:142900), an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by upper limb malformations, congenital heart defects, and CCS abnormalities (Basson et al., 1997; Li et al., 1997; Basson et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The cardiac phenotype of Holt–Oram syndrome, including atrioventricular conduction delay, has been recapitulated in Tbx5 heterozygous mice.
source: The cardiac phenotype of HOS, including atrioventricular conduction delay, has been recapitulated in the Tbx5 heterozygous mice (Bruneau et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: VCS-specific Tbx5 knockout caused slowed VCS function and ventricular tachycardia resulting in sudden death in mice.
source: Moreover, VCS-specific Tbx5 knockout caused slowed VCS function and ventricular tachycardia (VT) resulting in sudden death in mice (Arnolds et al., 2012), emphasizing the importance of Tbx5 in VCS conduction.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Tbx5 is strongly expressed in the atria and VCS.
source: Tbx5 is strongly expressed in the atria and VCS (Arnolds et al., 2012; Moskowitz et al., 2007; Moskowitz et al., 2004; Bakker et al., 2008), and directly regulates several targets required for VCS function (Moskowitz et al., 2007; Bruneau et al., 2001; Hiroi et al., 2001), including Gja5 (Cx40) (Bruneau et al., 2001) and Scn5a (Nav1.5) (Arnolds et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Tbx5 directly regulates Gja5 (Cx40).
source: Tbx5 is strongly expressed in the atria and VCS (Arnolds et al., 2012; Moskowitz et al., 2007; Moskowitz et al., 2004; Bakker et al., 2008), and directly regulates several targets required for VCS function (Moskowitz et al., 2007; Bruneau et al., 2001; Hiroi et al., 2001), including Gja5 (Cx40) (Bruneau et al., 2001) and Scn5a (Nav1.5) (Arnolds et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Tbx5 directly regulates Scn5a (Nav1.5).
source: Tbx5 is strongly expressed in the atria and VCS (Arnolds et al., 2012; Moskowitz et al., 2007; Moskowitz et al., 2004; Bakker et al., 2008), and directly regulates several targets required for VCS function (Moskowitz et al., 2007; Bruneau et al., 2001; Hiroi et al., 2001), including Gja5 (Cx40) (Bruneau et al., 2001) and Scn5a (Nav1.5) (Arnolds et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Tbx3 encodes a T-box transcriptional repressor which is critical for cardiac development.
source: Tbx3 encodes a T-box transcriptional repressor which is critical for cardiac development (Bakker et al., 2008; Frank et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Dominant mutations in human TBX3 cause Ulnar–Mammary syndrome.
source: Dominant mutations in human TBX3 cause Ulnar–Mammary syndrome (OMIM:181450), a developmental disorder (Meneghini et al., 2006; Bamshad et al., 1997), that includes functional conduction system defects (Linden et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Ulnar–Mammary syndrome includes functional conduction system defects.
source: Dominant mutations in human TBX3 cause Ulnar–Mammary syndrome (OMIM:181450), a developmental disorder (Meneghini et al., 2006; Bamshad et al., 1997), that includes functional conduction system defects (Linden et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Tbx3 is specifically expressed within CCS.
source: In the heart, Tbx3 is specifically expressed within CCS (Bakker et al., 2008; Hoogaars et al., 2004), and its deficiency below critical level leads to lethal arrhythmias (Frank et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Tbx3 deficiency below critical level leads to lethal arrhythmias.
source: In the heart, Tbx3 is specifically expressed within CCS (Bakker et al., 2008; Hoogaars et al., 2004), and its deficiency below critical level leads to lethal arrhythmias (Frank et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Tbx3 is required for the molecular identity but not the function of the VCS.
source: Furthermore, Tbx3 is required for the molecular identity but not the function of the VCS (Bakker et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Tbx3 in SAN and AVN is required for their proper function.
source: In contrast, Tbx3 in SAN and AVN is required for their proper function (Hoogaars et al., 2004), emphasizing its critical role in maintaining proper cardiac rhythm.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The adult VCS-specific removal of TBX5 shifted the fast VCS into a slow nodal-like system.
source: The adult VCS-specific removal of TBX5 or overexpression of TBX3 shifted the fast VCS into a slow nodal-like system, indicating that the Tbx3/Tbx5 ratio determines nodal versus VCS function (Burnicka-Turek et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Overexpression of TBX3 in the adult VCS shifted the fast VCS into a slow nodal-like system.
source: The adult VCS-specific removal of TBX5 or overexpression of TBX3 shifted the fast VCS into a slow nodal-like system, indicating that the Tbx3/Tbx5 ratio determines nodal versus VCS function (Burnicka-Turek et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The Tbx3/Tbx5 ratio determines nodal versus VCS function.
source: The adult VCS-specific removal of TBX5 or overexpression of TBX3 shifted the fast VCS into a slow nodal-like system, indicating that the Tbx3/Tbx5 ratio determines nodal versus VCS function (Burnicka-Turek et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: A novel compound Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional allele was generated.
source: To investigate the consequences of Tbx3 and Tbx5 compound removal from the mature VCS, we generated a novel compound Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional allele.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and detailed in Figure 1 and supplementary figures.

claim: VCS-specific genetic removal of both TBX3 and TBX5 transformed fast-conducting adult VCS into working myocardium-like cardiomyocytes.
source: We found that VCS-specific genetic removal of both TBX3 and TBX5 transformed fast-conducting, adult VCS into working myocardium-like cardiomyocytes, shifting them from conduction to non-conduction myocytes.
evidence: This is a main conclusion stated in the introduction based on the experimental findings.

claim: Tbx3 resides at mm39 chr5:119808734–119822789.
source: Tbx3 and Tbx5 reside in cis on mouse chromosome 5 (Tbx3 mm39 chr5:119808734–119822789; Tbx5 mm39 chr5:119970733–120023284).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific genomic coordinates.

claim: Tbx5 resides at mm39 chr5:119970733–120023284.
source: Tbx3 and Tbx5 reside in cis on mouse chromosome 5 (Tbx3 mm39 chr5:119808734–119822789; Tbx5 mm39 chr5:119970733–120023284).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific genomic coordinates.

claim: The Tbx5 floxed allele was targeted using the CRISPR–Cas9 system in the background of a previously validated Tbx3 floxed allele.
source: Therefore, to generate a double-conditional knockout, we targeted Tbx5 in the background of a previously validated Tbx3 floxed allele (Frank et al., 2011) using the CRISPR–Cas9 system (Gurumurthy et al., 2021; Dow et al., 2015; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The engineered Tbx5 floxed allele mirrors a previously published allele.
source: We engineered a Tbx5 floxed allele mirroring a previously published allele (Bruneau et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: Loss of both Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression was observed in the VCS of adult Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional mutant mice at the protein level.
source: We observed loss of both Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression, on both the mRNA and protein levels, in the VCS of adult Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional mutant mice (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) but not in their littermate controls (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Loss of both Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression was observed in the VCS of adult Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional mutant mice at the mRNA level.
source: We observed loss of both Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression, on both the mRNA and protein levels, in the VCS of adult Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional mutant mice (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) but not in their littermate controls (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) (Figure 1B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Partial loss of Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression in the adult VCS of Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional heterozygous mice was observed.
source: Partial loss of Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression in the adult VCS of Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional heterozygous mice (Tbx3fl/+;Tbx5fl/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) was observed compared to littermate controls (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression remained similar in the atrial and ventricular myocardium of all allelic combinations, including Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice.
source: Consistent with the VCS selectivity of Cre activity in the MinKCreERT2 mice (Arnolds and Moskowitz, 2011b), Tbx3 and Tbx5 expression remained similar in the atrial and ventricular myocardium of all allelic combinations, including Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: All tamoxifen-treated Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ mice died suddenly within 3 months post-tamoxifen administration.
source: Within the 3 months post-tamoxifen administration, all tamoxifen-treated Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl; R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ mice had died suddenly (n = 40).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: No mortality was observed among tamoxifen-treated Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ littermates during the 3 months post-tamoxifen period.
source: In contrast, no mortality was observed among the tamoxifen-treated Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ or Tbx3fl/+;Tbx5fl/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ littermates (each cohort n = 40) during this period (Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.0001; Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional heterozygous mice p < 0.0001, log-rank test; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: No mortality was observed among tamoxifen-treated Tbx3fl/+;Tbx5fl/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ littermates during the 3 months post-tamoxifen period.
source: In contrast, no mortality was observed among the tamoxifen-treated Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ or Tbx3fl/+;Tbx5fl/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ littermates (each cohort n = 40) during this period (Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.0001; Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional heterozygous mice p < 0.0001, log-rank test; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Double deletion of Tbx3 and Tbx5 from the adult VCS causes lethality beginning at 3 weeks post-tamoxifen.
source: These results revealed that double deletion of Tbx3 and Tbx5 from the adult VCS causes lethality beginning at 3 weeks post-tamoxifen.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the mortality data.

claim: VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 deficiency caused profound conduction slowing in Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ mice.
source: VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 deficiency caused profound conduction slowing in Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ mice by ambulatory telemetry electrocardiography (ECG) analysis compared to Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional heterozygous mice (Tbx3fl/+;Tbx5fl/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) and littermate controls (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) (Figure 2A–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The PR interval was significantly prolonged in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice compared to controls.
source: Specifically, the PR interval, representing the period between atrial and ventricular depolarization, and the QRS duration, indicating the length of ventricular depolarization and early repolarization in mice, were both significantly prolonged (Figure 2A, B, D; PR: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test; QRS: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The QRS duration was significantly prolonged in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice compared to controls.
source: Specifically, the PR interval, representing the period between atrial and ventricular depolarization, and the QRS duration, indicating the length of ventricular depolarization and early repolarization in mice, were both significantly prolonged (Figure 2A, B, D; PR: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test; QRS: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Episodes of spontaneous VT were observed in four out of seven Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ mice.
source: Ambulatory studies revealed episodes of spontaneous VT in four out of seven Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ mice, in contrast to none observed in seven littermate controls (Figure 2G, p < 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice showed significantly increased susceptibility to VT following burst stimulation.
source: Furthermore, Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) showed significantly increased susceptibility to VT following burst stimulation in invasive electrophysiology (EP) studies (three of three Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+ mice vs. zero of seven littermate controls; Figure 2H, p < 0.05, Welch t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 2H.

claim: VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional heterozygous mice showed neither conduction nor electrophysiological defects.
source: In contrast, VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional heterozygous mice (n = 7) showed neither conduction nor electrophysiological defects (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: No changes in the refractory/recovery periods of atrium, ventricle, or nodes were detected in experimental and control mice.
source: Consistent with the use of a VCS-specific Cre (MinKCreERT2), no changes in the refractory/recovery periods of atrium, ventricle, or nodes (atrial effective refractory period, ventricular effective refractory period (VERP), atrioventricular nodal effective refractory period, or sinus node recovery time) were detected by intracardiac EP conducted on experimental and control mice (Figure 2I, p < 0.05, Welch t-test).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Transthoracic echocardiography revealed no significant differences in left ventricular ejection fraction between VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5-deficient and control mice.
source: Transthoracic echocardiography revealed no significant differences in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and fractional shortening (FS) between VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5-deficient (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) and control (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) mice (LVEF: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test; and FS: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p > 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test; Figure 3A, B, D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Transthoracic echocardiography revealed no significant differences in fractional shortening between VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5-deficient and control mice.
source: Transthoracic echocardiography revealed no significant differences in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and fractional shortening (FS) between VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5-deficient (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) and control (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) mice (LVEF: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p < 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test; and FS: Tbx3:Tbx5 double-conditional knockout mice vs. control mice p > 0.05, n = 7, Welch t-test; Figure 3A, B, D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Histological examination demonstrated no discernible differences between VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout and control mice.
source: Histological examination of all four chambers demonstrated no discernible differences between VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl; R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) and control (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+; MinKCreERT2/+) mice, nor between the double-knockout (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+; MinKCreERT2/+) and single-knockout models for either Tbx3 (Tbx3fl/fl;Tbx5+/+;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+) or Tbx5 (Tbx3+/+;Tbx5fl/fl;R26ReYFP/+;MinKCreERT2/+).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3G-K.

claim: Ventricular muscle appeared normal without hypertrophy or myofibrillar disarray in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout mice.
source: Ventricular muscle appeared normal without hypertrophy or myofibrillar disarray, and no fibrosis was present (Figure 3G, I–K, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: No fibrosis was present in Tbx3:Tbx5 double-knockout mice.
source: Ventricular muscle appeared normal without hypertrophy or myofibrillar disarray, and no fibrosis was present (Figure 3G, I–K, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis confirmed no fibrosis in VCS of Tbx3:Tbx5-deficient mice.
source: qRT-PCR analysis for fibrosis genes Col1a1 (Pan et al., 2022; Hua et al., 2020; Zhao et al., 2018) and Postn (Zhao et al., 2018; Ackerman et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024; Oka et al., 2007) further confirmed no fibrosis in VCS of Tbx3:Tbx5-deficient mice (Figure 3L).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3L.

claim: The conduction defect and VT in mice with VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 deletion occur prior to the onset of left ventricular dysfunction or evidence of remodeling.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that the conduction defect and VT observed in mice with VCS-specific Tbx3:Tbx5 deletion (Figure 2) occur prior to the onset of left ventricular (LV) dysfunction or evidence of remodeling (Figure 3), implying a primary origin.
